risks: Absolute revenue remains small despite high growth rates.
A major demand partner underperformed expectations, demonstrating utilization and customer-demand risk despite fleet scale.
Human couriers, e-bikes, drones and other autonomous systems remain substitutes; local density and operating-domain constraints can shift the bottleneck from autonomy to utilization.
Absolute revenue remains small, increasing financing sensitivity while the network is scaled.
Demand concentration and platform bargaining power can impair utilization and pricing even if robot technology performs.
Q2 cost of revenues of $12.017M materially exceeded $3.238M of revenue, producing an $8.779M gross loss; rapid top-line growth has not yet established positive gross economics.
The guidance reduction explicitly identifies lower-than-expected Uber Eats volume, demonstrating material platform-demand dependence even as DoorDash and other verticals diversify the network.

Reported revenue remains small relative to the expense base, and lower-than-expected Uber Eats delivery volume demonstrates demand/partner concentration and utilization risk despite rapid year-over-year growth.

Dependence on partner delivery volume can produce utilization and revenue volatility, while the current revenue base remains small relative to operating expense and sustainable per-robot economics are not yet demonstrated.
Breadth across delivery, hospital robotics, hardware and advertising increases integration and execution complexity.
Merchant availability is not equivalent to order volume, utilization or profitable unit economics.
Breadth across delivery geographies, merchant hardware, advertising and hospital robotics can raise integration and capital-allocation complexity before unit economics by channel are demonstrated.
Merchant availability may be mistaken for demand or profitable scale if order density, utilization and contribution margin are not separately verified.
Absolute revenue remains small relative to the company's operating-expense base.
The large revenue-guidance reset demonstrates material demand/execution uncertainty despite fleet and partnership expansion.
The company cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $9-$10 million because Uber Eats delivery volume was below expectations and projected second-half demand was removed.
Lower delivery volume through Uber Eats demonstrates customer/channel concentration and demand-conversion risk.
Merchant availability does not establish order density, revenue per robot or profitable utilization.
Multiple simultaneous initiatives increase execution complexity while Q2 guidance already showed demand-conversion risk.
Improving mix does not establish positive gross profit dollars, operating leverage or fleet-level profitability.
Liquidity supports execution runway but does not prove that diversified pilots convert into profitable utilization.
Absolute revenue remains small relative to liquidity and deployment ambitions; equity count was approximately 86 million shares at June 30, 2026.
Partner demand concentration and utilization can cause deployed fleet capacity to under-monetize.
Continued reliance on equity funding before durable positive unit economics can transfer commercialization risk to shareholders through dilution.

Headline deployed-fleet and merchant counts can overstate economic progress if utilization and contribution economics remain weak.
